evals.prompt: I'm building an AI job matcher. It reads my achievements.md and scores job listings for fit. I want to set up some kind of loop so that when I apply to a job and don't hear back, that signal helps improve the scoring. How do I structure this?
evals.expected_output: Identifies this as a win/loss + prompt-improvement loop combination. Fills out the full TRIGGER/ACTION/SELF-EVAL/OUTPUT anatomy. Recommends building outcome capture before improving the scorer. Gives a concrete first step for this week.
assertions: Names a specific loop type (win/loss or outcome loop or similar) — not generic advice
Writes out the TRIGGER / ACTION / SELF-EVAL / OUTPUT anatomy explicitly
Recommends capturing the outcome signal (applied Y/N, response Y/N) as the first build step
Gives a concrete actionable next step, not a list of options
Mentions connecting outcome data back to scoring — the feedback-as-engine concept

evals.prompt: my prompt for picking resume bullets keeps producing mediocre results. i've tried tweaking it a few times but i can't tell if it's actually getting better or if i'm just fooling myself. what loop should i set up?
evals.expected_output: Immediately identifies this as a prompt-improvement loop. Explains that the user needs evals before they can know if the prompt improved. Gives a concrete LLM-as-judge rubric design. Explains the loop anatomy for prompt improvement. Does not give a list of 5 options.
assertions: Names 'prompt-improvement loop' specifically — not a generic feedback loop
Points out that the user needs evals (golden test set) to measure improvement — this is the root cause
Provides or describes a concrete LLM judge rubric (not just 'rate 1-5')
Writes the loop anatomy: trigger → run evals → rewrite prompt → re-eval → compare delta → stop condition
Gives a specific stop condition (e.g. pass rate threshold, not 'until it feels good')

evals.prompt: I'm a PM on an AI writing assistant. We ship updates every 2 weeks. I want to set up loops across our whole product process — discovery, building, and staying on top of things. Where do I even start? I feel like there's too much to do at once.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the situation (overwhelmed, wants full-stack loops). Recommends starting with ONE loop — the prompt-improvement or ship-check loop for Build & Ship since they're already shipping. Explains all three categories but is opinionated about prioritization. Does not dump all 20+ loops on the user.
assertions: Does not list all 20+ loops — is selective and opinionated
Recommends starting with exactly one loop, not three
Explains the three categories (Product & Discovery, Build & Ship, Personal & Ops) briefly
Justifies the recommended starting loop with a reason tied to the user's context (2-week ship cadence)
Ends with a concrete this-week action, not a framework overview
